    How customer reviews and ratings work

    Customer reviews, including Product Star Ratings, help customers to learn more about the product and decide whether it is the right product for them.

    To calculate the overall star rating and percentage breakdown by star, we do not use a simple average. Instead, our system considers things such as how recent a review is and if the reviewer bought the item on Amazon. It also analyses reviews to verify trustworthiness.

      4 out of 5 stars
      Good picture quality overall but disappointing local dimming and black levels
      Reviewed in India on 30 October 2026
      Display Size: 55.0 InchesSet name: 2026 Series
      Verified Purchase
      Brief content visible, double tap to read full content.
      Full content visible, double tap to read brief content.

      Good picture quality overall, but disappointing local dimming and black levels

      I've been using the Samsung M2EH 55-inch Mini LED TV, and my experience has been mixed. The TV has several good qualities, but its backlight performance and blooming are disappointing, especially if you're particular about picture quality in dark scenes.

      What I liked:

      The picture is good overall. Colours look good, clarity is good, and motion handling is decent. For regular TV viewing, YouTube and OTT content, it can deliver an enjoyable viewing experience. If you're looking for a branded Samsung TV with a good-looking picture for everyday use, this TV has its strengths.

      I haven't tested the gaming features because I don't own a gaming console, so I can't comment on gaming performance.

      The biggest disappointment: black levels and blooming

      Samsung advertises this TV as Mini LED and uses the term Supreme Mini LED Dimming. However, in my experience, its local-dimming performance doesn't deliver the kind of contrast I expected from a Mini LED television.

      Dark scenes can look cloudy and grey, with noticeable blooming around bright objects. I couldn't find a manual local-dimming control that would let me adjust the effect to my preference. The overall experience doesn't give me the deep blacks and precise backlight control I associate with a good full-array local-dimming television.

      To be fair, I use and LG C1 OLED, and I've also seen Samsung Neo QLED and other Mini LED televisions in showrooms. That has given me a higher benchmark for black levels and contrast. Compared with those experiences, the M2EH feels underwhelming in dark scenes. Other Mini LED televisions around a similar price can offer a more convincing local-dimming experience, although I haven't conducted a direct, controlled comparison.

      Picture mode recommendation

      My advice is to try Dynamic, Standard and Movie modes rather than automatically choosing Filmmaker Mode.

      On my TV, Filmmaker Mode makes the picture look particularly gloomy and cloudy in dark scenes. Dynamic mode makes the picture brighter and more watchable for me, while Standard and Movie are also worth trying.

      This is my personal experience, and results may vary depending on room lighting, content and individual picture settings.

      Is it really Mini LED?

      The TV is marketed as Mini LED, but the real-world picture experience doesn't meet my expectations for that technology. Samsung's advertised dimming terminology doesn't tell buyers how many independently controlled zones are available or how effectively they work.

      I wouldn't buy this TV expecting the same black levels, contrast or blooming control as a good full-array Mini LED or Neo QLED television. The picture can look good, but its backlight performance is a significant limitation for someone who watches a lot of dark, cinematic content.

      Final verdict

      If you want a Samsung-branded 55-inch 4K TV with good colours, clarity, motion and enjoyable everyday picture quality, this TV may suit you.

      However, if you're buying it specifically for Mini LED performance, deep blacks, excellent HDR contrast and minimal blooming, I recommend comparing it with competing Mini LED models before purchasing.

      My biggest advice: don't judge this TV by its Mini LED branding alone. Test the dark-scene performance in person and compare all the picture modes. For me, the picture is good in many situations, but the local-dimming performance is the biggest weakness.
